subtitle: A SideFX Training Series
thesis: The future of agentic engineering is centered on what agents are allowed to mean, produce, execute, and change.
audience: Engineers, operators, architects, and product owners building dependable agentic systems.
editorialRules: Human problem leads; capsule identity anchors the lesson.
Every episode uses the same ten training sections.
Input, Event, and Outcome change human experience and visible relationships.
Source authority, observed local inspection, and fictional staging remain distinguishable.
Contemporary comparisons use a specific cited system or an explicitly illustrative design.
Demonstrated decision output never implies live effect enforcement.
An episode ends with a question that leads into the next capability.
Each episode distinguishes What exists, What should exist, and What is missing.
Current evidence uses solid source-linked lines; target architecture uses luminous outlines; missing closure uses interrupted boundaries.
Target experience must remain visible even if current mechanics are incomplete; gaps feed platform improvement testimony.

episodes.title: When the Agent Is Ready to Act, Who Decides?
episodes.objective: Distinguish present decision semantics from the intended live enforcement boundary and its closure evidence.
episodes.exercise: Resolve an out-of-scope publication to a permitted inspection, then identify the live evidence needed to establish the target boundary.
episodes.takeaway: The agent proposes the action. Authority decides what may cross into execution.

episodes.title: Can You Approve What You Cannot See?
episodes.objective: Trace a human review from capsule meaning to a faithful projection and an explicit review disposition.
episodes.exercise: Identify one misleading scene, trace it to authority, and propose a bounded correction.
episodes.takeaway: Make meaning visible enough for a human to challenge it.

episodes.title: Many Models. Who Runs the Work?
episodes.objective: Explain role eligibility, isolated context, output validation, and deterministic continuation.
episodes.exercise: Predict which dependent stages remain held after a reviewer output fails its contract.
episodes.takeaway: Models contribute within roles; the admitted plan controls continuation.

episodes.title: The Provider Changed. What Must Stay?
episodes.objective: Identify the meaning, context, budget, and identity that a permitted provider switch must preserve.
episodes.exercise: Choose the first eligible alternative from an ordered policy and explain why a cheaper incompatible model is rejected.
episodes.takeaway: Replace the provider only while preserving the role's obligations.

episodes.title: The Rebuild Failed. Did We Lose Our Work?
episodes.objective: Distinguish performing rollback from verifying preservation through before-and-after digest facts.
episodes.exercise: Find one altered untargeted artifact in a digest comparison and withhold the preservation claim.
episodes.takeaway: Verify that approved work survived before calling recovery complete.

episodes.title: What Makes Intelligence Portable?
episodes.objective: Explain content addressing, minimum sufficient representation, deterministic reveal, and admission boundaries.
episodes.exercise: Choose the representation required for a review and identify what the capsule alone does not authorize.
episodes.takeaway: A capsule preserves capability identity; possession does not grant authority.

episodes.title: When Agents Disagree, What Decides?
episodes.objective: Interpret normalized conformance findings and ADVANCED, REPAIRABLE, or BLOCKED round outcomes.
episodes.exercise: Map a duplicate semantic realization to the bounded repair surface rather than soliciting a majority vote.
episodes.takeaway: Conformance evidence resolves the round; agreement is not proof.

episodes.title: Green Tests. Why Is It Still Not Published?
episodes.objective: Explain sealed baseline comparison, renewed proof, atomic admission, and publication lineage.
episodes.exercise: Respond to a changed mainline baseline without relabeling local proof as a published result.
episodes.takeaway: Publication needs the exact change to survive its shared authority boundary.

episodes.title: Can the Claim Survive Inspection?
episodes.objective: Separate VERIFIED, INTEGRITY_REJECTED, and NOT_OBSERVABLE when tracing a receipt chain.
episodes.exercise: Classify a missing generation separately from a digest mismatch.
episodes.takeaway: Missing evidence and broken integrity are different facts.

episodes.title: The Model Answered. Who Decides What Counts?
episodes.objective: Trace one governed attempt from request and provider binding to normalized testimony and failure evidence.
episodes.exercise: Identify what a schema-valid model response proves and what still requires admission.
episodes.takeaway: A model response is attributable testimony, not self-authorizing truth.
